sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余烬》。

sentences.en: For bonus episodes, early access, ad-free listening and access to our chat community, please sign up at restishistorypod.com.
sentences.zh: 欢迎前往 restishistorypod.com 注册，以获取独家番外、抢先收听、无广告体验以及我们的聊天社群权限。

sentences.en: Or if you're listening on the Apple Podcasts app, you can subscribe within the app in just a few clicks.
sentences.zh: 或者，如果您使用的是 Apple Podcasts App，只需点击几下即可在应用内订阅。

sentences.en: Hello, welcome to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听《历史的余烬》。

sentences.en: For more than 200 episodes, we've covered everything from the foundations of ancient Babylon to the origins of the war in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 在过去两百多期节目中，我们无所不谈，从古巴比伦的奠基到乌克兰战争的起源。

sentences.en: But no topic has excited more interest, enthusiasm and curiosity among the great British public than today's.
sentences.zh: 但没有哪个话题能像今天这样，在广大英国听众中激起如此高涨的兴趣、热情和好奇心。

sentences.en: One of the truly great questions of history.
sentences.zh: 这是历史上真正伟大的问题之一。

sentences.en: What has been the importance, the influence and the impact of the pigeon?
sentences.zh: 鸽子的重要性、影响力和冲击力究竟体现在哪里？

sentences.en: Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 我是汤姆·霍兰。

sentences.en: I'm so excited about this episode.
sentences.zh: 我对这一期节目感到无比兴奋。

sentences.en: You know, I think it was January was it?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我想那是在一月吧？

sentences.en: I raised it.
sentences.zh: 是我提出来的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I suggested doing it.
sentences.zh: 对，我建议做这个主题的。

sentences.en: Seems like years ago, frankly, Tom.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，汤姆，感觉好像已经过去好几年了。

sentences.en: Yeah, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 是的，多米尼克。

sentences.en: So you, I think it's fair to say, have treated initially this subject with levity.
sentences.zh: 所以我想说，一开始你对这个主题的态度可以说是相当轻浮的。

sentences.en: You did not regard it as a fit subject for historical inquiry.
sentences.zh: 你根本没把它当成一个适合进行历史探讨的正经课题。

sentences.en: That is an outrageous claim, Tom, and one I absolutely reject.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这是一个离谱的指控，我绝对不接受。

sentences.en: Well, Dominic, I have the, I don't actually have the evidence to prove it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，多米尼克，我有……其实我没有直接证据来证明这一点。

sentences.en: You have the documentary evidence to prove it.
sentences.zh: 你有文件证据来证明。

sentences.en: I'm sure there are the old tweet or something out there with you sneering at it as a subject.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，网上还能找到你当年对这个主题冷嘲热讽的旧推文什么的。

sentences.en: But, but, but we have both agreed, haven't we, that actually the relationship of humans to animals, to creatures is a really fascinating one.
sentences.zh: 但是，但是，但是我们俩都同意过，不是吗？实际上人类与动物、与生物之间的关系是一个非常迷人的课题。

sentences.en: So we've talked about doing, um, horses, dogs.
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论过做关于马、狗的主题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And dogs, of course, have been a constant theme of our early episode.
sentences.zh: 而且毫无疑问，狗一直是我们早期节目的一个贯穿主题。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Dogs were killed, weren't they?
sentences.zh: 狗都被写死了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, they're dead dogs for a while, which is a shame.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有段时间总有死狗出现，这挺遗憾的。

sentences.en: But today we're going to have dead pigeons.
sentences.zh: 但今天我们要讲死鸽子。

sentences.en: And so the reason I thought that actually, um, together with horses and dogs, pigeons are probably, um, the most interesting animals to look at in terms
sentences.zh: 所以，我之所以认为除了马和狗之外，鸽子可能也是最有趣的动物主题之一，

sentences.en: of how humans have understood them, the uses that humans have put them to.
sentences.zh: 在于人类是如何理解它们的，以及人类是如何利用它们的。

sentences.en: And also I kind of, perhaps the, the darkest theme of all, um, the, the way in which humans have, um, impacted and eaten them.
sentences.zh: 而且我还觉得，也许其中最黑暗的主题是，人类对它们产生的影响以及将它们吃掉的方式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, have, have, have shot and wiped them out as well.
sentences.zh: 还有把它们开枪打死并赶尽杀绝。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So extinction is also a part of the history of humanity's relationship to animals.
sentences.zh: 所以物种灭绝也是人类与动物关系史的一部分。

sentences.en: However, so the reason why I thought we should do pigeons is because I went to an Advent service, um, last year and there I
sentences.zh: 不过，我之所以觉得我们应该做鸽子，是因为去年我参加了一场将临期礼拜活动，在那里

sentences.en: found myself sitting next to Gordon Carrera, um, the BBC security correspondent, author of many
sentences.zh: 我发现自己竟然坐在戈登·卡雷拉旁边，他就是BBC的安全事务记者，著有多本

sentences.en: fantastic books on history of security services, all that kind of stuff, presenter of TV programs on MI5, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 关于安全机构历史等方面的精彩书籍，还是MI5等电视节目的主持人。

sentences.en: But he told me that he had written a book, which I had missed called Operation Columba,
sentences.zh: 但他告诉我，他写过一本书，而我之前错过了，书名叫《哥伦巴行动》，

sentences.en: the secret pigeon service, the untold story of world war two resistance in Europe, that as it suggests has pigeons absolutely at its heart.
sentences.zh: 即秘密鸽子服务：二战欧洲抵抗运动中不为人知的故事。正如书名所示，鸽子在其中绝对处于核心地位。

sentences.en: And Gordon said, you must do pigeons.
sentences.zh: 戈登说，你们一定要做一期关于鸽子的节目。

sentences.en: So Gordon, the time has come.
sentences.zh: 所以，戈登，时机已到。

sentences.en: We are doing pigeons.
sentences.zh: 我们正在做鸽子。

sentences.en: Should we welcome you with a sort of a pigeon style coup or something?
sentences.zh: 我们是不是该用某种咕咕叫的鸽子姿态来欢迎你？

sentences.en: Well, thank you.
sentences.zh: 好吧，谢谢。

sentences.en: I've never been called that before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从来没被人这样称呼过。

sentences.en: I'm so grateful for coming on because, um, I'm very excited about pigeons.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢能来参加节目，因为我对鸽子充满了热情。

sentences.en: I did sense that there might be some people out there who might think it wasn't a, a worthy subject for such a lofty,
sentences.zh: 我确实隐约感觉到，有些人可能会觉得这不是一个配得上我们这个崇高、

sentences.en: high-minded podcaSt. So I'm looking forward for the chance to kind of make the case for pigeons.
sentences.zh: 有内涵的播客的 worthy（值得探讨的）主题。所以我很期待有机会为鸽子正名。

sentences.en: In my mind is the superheroes of history.
sentences.zh: 在我心目中，它们是历史上的超级英雄。

sentences.en: Oh, that's a big claim.
sentences.zh: 哦，这可真是个惊人的说法。

sentences.en: Who saved us in the past and may even save us in the future.
sentences.zh: 它们在过去拯救了我们，甚至可能在未来拯救我们。

sentences.en: That's, that's the claim I'm going to make.
sentences.zh: 这就是我要提出的观点。

sentences.en: So maybe you could start off.
sentences.zh: 所以也许你可以先给我们讲讲。

sentences.en: I mean, I notoriously know nothing and take no interest in science or the natural world at all.
sentences.zh: 我的大名在外，我对科学或自然界一无所知，也完全不感兴趣。

sentences.en: So for an absolute ignoramus like me, what is a pigeon?
sentences.zh: 所以对于像我这样的绝对无知者来说，到底什么是鸽子？

sentences.en: Good question to start with.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的开场问题。

sentences.en: The first thing to say is that what we call a pigeon and what we think of as a pigeon around us is actually a dove.
sentences.zh: 首先要说明的是，我们所说的鸽子以及身边的鸽子，实际上是一种鸠（dove）。

sentences.en: And basically doves have good PR.
sentences.zh: 基本上，鸠（doves）的公众形象很好。

sentences.en: Pigeons have bad PR.
sentences.zh: 而鸽子（pigeons）的公众形象很差。

sentences.en: But the pigeon, the one we think of is the rock dove.
sentences.zh: 但我们通常所指的那种鸽子是原鸽（rock dove）。

sentences.en: And there are other types of pigeons as well.
sentences.zh: 还有其他种类的鸽子。

sentences.en: And we might come to some of those, the kind of passenger pigeon and, you know, the wood pigeon and different types.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会聊到其中一些，比如旅鸽、林鸽以及其他不同品种。

sentences.en: But Columbolivia is the kind of famous pigeon.
sentences.zh: 但原鸽才是那种著名的鸽子。

sentences.en: And what's the name, what makes it really interesting and unusual is, is that it's very friendly with people.
sentences.zh: 是什么让它变得非常有趣且与众不同呢？那就是它对人类非常友好。

sentences.en: So, so first of all, rock dove, because it doesn't so much nest in trees, but it loves rocky ledges.
sentences.zh: 首先，原鸽不太在树上筑巢，它们更喜欢岩石峭壁。

sentences.en: So originally cliffs.
sentences.zh: 所以最初它们生活在悬崖上。

sentences.en: But the fact that it was happy in cliffs meant it was quite happy on rocky ledges.
sentences.zh: 但它们在悬崖上生活得很自在，这意味着它们也很适应岩石峭壁。

sentences.en: So people found that they could build what became dove coats, you know, places where pigeons would quite happily come and live.
sentences.zh: 因此人们发现，他们可以建造后来的鸽舍，也就是鸽子会非常乐意前来安家落户的地方。

sentences.en: And also eventually you get plenty of rocky ledges in cities.
sentences.zh: 而且最终城市里也有了大量的岩石峭壁。

sentences.en: So that's why we see so many in the cities that they're intrinsically happy in a kind of human environment.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们在城市里能看到这么多鸽子，它们在人类环境中天生就感到快乐。

sentences.en: They're also very friendly with people.
sentences.zh: 它们对人类也非常友好。

sentences.en: They're not scared of us.
sentences.zh: 它们不怕我们。

sentences.en: You don't need to cage them.
sentences.zh: 你不需要把它们关在笼子里。

sentences.en: They'll come and eat out of your hand.
sentences.zh: 它们会过来吃你手里的食物。

sentences.en: And that means they're easy to domesticate.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它们很容易被驯化。

sentences.en: So right from the earliest days of history, it's meant they've been able to have this very interesting relationship with humans because they're friendly with us.
sentences.zh: 所以从历史的最早期开始，这就意味着它们能够与人类建立这种非常有趣的联系，因为它们对我们很友好。

sentences.en: They can be bred very easily for whatever reason, ranging from food to sport to their superpower, which hopefully we'll come to in a bit.
sentences.zh: 无论是出于食物、体育竞技，还是为了它们那希望我们一会儿会谈到的超能力，它们都可以非常容易地被繁育。

sentences.en: So Gordon, before we come on to that, the superpower and the uses that the pigeons have been put to by humans, could we,
sentences.zh: 所以戈登，在我们聊到那个之前——也就是超能力以及人类对鸽子的利用——我们能否……

sentences.en: you've talked about how humanity's relationship with the pigeon is very, very ancient.
sentences.zh: 你刚才谈到人类与鸽子的关系非常非常古老。

sentences.en: Could we just begin by looking at the, dare I say, sacral quality that the pigeon has had?
sentences.zh: 我们能否先来看看鸽子所具有的，请允许我这样说，神圣属性？

sentences.en: Well, because they are absolutely woven into some of the foundational mythologies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为它们确实被深深地编织进了一些奠基神话之中。

sentences.en: So the Bible, most obviously.
sentences.zh: 最明显的例子就是《圣经》。

sentences.en: So I guess probably the most famous episode in myth that pigeons have featured in is Noah and his Ark.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，鸽子在神话中出现的最著名情节大概就是诺亚方舟了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没准儿是的。

sentences.en: And if the story, of course, is that the birds are sent out and the raven is sent out and doesn't come back and the pigeon comes back with word that there's land.
sentences.zh: 这个故事当然是说，人们放出了鸟儿，乌鸦被放出去后没有回来，而鸽子带回了有陆地的消息。

sentences.en: It's one example of where one of the few examples where Game of Thrones is historically inaccurate, because, of course, in Game of Thrones, they use ravens to communicate.
sentences.zh: 这是《权力的游戏》在历史上不准确的少数几个例子之一，因为在《权力的游戏》中，他们是用乌鸦来传递信息的。

sentences.en: In reality, it was pigeons which would get sent out.
sentences.zh: 而在现实中，被放飞的其实是鸽子。

sentences.en: And if you look at Noah's Ark, it's the raven fails, but the pigeon, the dove, succeeds and brings back news.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看诺亚方舟的故事，乌鸦失败了，但鸽子——也就是鸠——成功了，并带回了消息。

sentences.en: And it's the association of pigeons with peace and chastity, which comes very early.
sentences.zh: 鸽子与和平、贞洁的联系非常早就建立起来了。

sentences.en: And this comes from people actually observing the mating rituals of the pigeons and how one of the reasons is just how affectionate they are with each other.
sentences.zh: 这来自于人们对鸽子求偶仪式的实际观察，其中原因之一就是它们彼此之间是多么深情。

sentences.en: And the male pigeon really will woo the female pigeon very attentively.
sentences.zh: 雄鸽确实会非常体贴地向雌鸽献殷勤。

sentences.en: And then the view from classical times onwards was that they became very chaste.
sentences.zh: 从古典时期开始，人们的看法就是它们变得非常纯洁。

sentences.en: They were very loyal to each other.
sentences.zh: 它们对彼此非常忠诚。

sentences.en: And so pigeons start to be seen as symbols of peace, of chastity, of fidelity.
sentences.zh: 因此，鸽子开始被视为和平、贞洁和忠贞的象征。

sentences.en: And you see that role as one part of their kind of spiritual role in the traditions and in many of the religious traditions around the world.
sentences.zh: 你会发现，这是它们在各种传统以及世界许多宗教传统中精神角色的一部分。

sentences.en: You see this in Christianity, you, of course, see the dove as the Holy Spirit descending from above.
sentences.zh: 你在基督教中也能看到这一点，你当然会看到作为圣灵从天而降的白鸽。

sentences.en: The Holy Spirit comes down as a dove.
sentences.zh: 圣灵化作一只鸽子降临。

sentences.en: You also see them used as animal sacrifices in religion.
sentences.zh: 你还会看到它们在宗教中被用作动物祭品。

sentences.en: But Gordon, a very stupid question to, again, reflect my natural history ignorance.
sentences.zh: 但戈登，为了再次反映我自然历史知识的匮乏，我有一个非常愚蠢的问题。

sentences.en: So why are they called doves?
sentences.zh: 为什么它们被称为“鸠（doves）”？

sentences.en: So no one talks about, I mean, if somebody said the Holy Spirit, the pigeon of the Holy Spirit, I mean, that sounds faintly comical.
sentences.zh: 所以没有人会说……我的意思是，如果有人说圣灵，圣灵之鸽，听起来会有点滑稽。

sentences.en: But the dove, you know, sounds, we take it for granted.
sentences.zh: 但“鸠（dove）”这个词听起来……我们觉得理所当然。

sentences.en: So why the branding?
sentences.zh: 所以为什么要这样包装？

sentences.en: Well, the branding is just unfortunate branding to some extent.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从某种程度上说，这种包装只是一种不幸的包装。

sentences.en: And I think the pigeon has just had bad, bad PR.
sentences.zh: 我认为鸽子只是拥有了糟糕的公众形象。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are differences and there are different types of doves.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，它们之间存在差异，也有不同种类的鸠。

sentences.en: But I would make the case that in many cases in history where they are talking about doves, they're really talking about pigeons.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，在历史上很多提到鸠的地方，它们实际上指的就是鸽子。

sentences.en: Now, that may not always be the case.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并不总是如此。

sentences.en: So your message to the Church of England is, you know, amplify pigeons.
sentences.zh: 所以你给英格兰教会的信息是，你知道的，大力宣传鸽子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Big up the pigeons, play down the doves.
sentences.zh: 大肆宣扬鸽子，淡化鸠。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: And they become this symbol of peace as well as chastity.
sentences.zh: 它们成为了和平以及贞洁的象征。

sentences.en: And one of the interesting ways that's used is that they're kind of released and we still see them released.
sentences.zh: 其中一个有趣的用法是它们被放飞，我们现在仍然能看到它们被放飞。

sentences.en: You see the kind of doves or white pigeons released famously at Olympic ceremonies.
sentences.zh: 你会看到在奥运会开幕式上，人们习惯性地放飞各种鸠或白鸽。

sentences.en: And this happens in ancient times.
sentences.zh: 这在古代就有了。

sentences.en: It's revived in the modern Olympics.
sentences.zh: 并在现代奥运会上得以恢复。

sentences.en: One of the slight tragedies, though, comes in the Seoul Olympics in 1988.
sentences.zh: 不过，其中一个小小的悲剧发生在1988年首尔奥运会上。

sentences.en: It flew into the flame, didn't they?
sentences.zh: 它们飞进圣火里去了，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm afraid so.
sentences.zh: 恐怕是的。

sentences.en: They didn't fly home, but they just settled on the nearest rocky ledge, which unfortunately was the Olympic flame, which then got turned on and then grilled the pigeons.
sentences.zh: 它们没有飞回家，而是落在了最近的岩石峭壁上，不幸的是，那是奥运圣火，随后圣火被点燃，然后把鸽子给烤了。

sentences.en: So essentially in antiquity, there are the two themes.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上在古代，有两个主题。

sentences.en: There's the homing pigeon.
sentences.zh: 一个是信鸽。

sentences.en: So as in Noah sending the dove out and it comes back.
sentences.zh: 就像诺亚放出鸽子然后它飞回来一样。

sentences.en: And then there's this idea of it being monogamous, of being a symbol of lifelong chastity and love.
sentences.zh: 另一个是它是一夫一妻制的，是终身贞洁和爱情的象征。

sentences.en: And you can see that both of those, I guess, would, I mean, there's lots of potential there for myth making.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以看到，这两者都……我的意思是，那里有很多适合神话创作的潜力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And you see it in Egyptian mythology, in Greek mythology, you see it in the major modern religious traditions.
sentences.zh: 你在埃及神话、希腊神话中都能看到这一点，在各大现代宗教传统中也能看到。

sentences.en: All of them will use pigeons in different ways.
sentences.zh: 它们都会以不同的方式使用鸽子。

sentences.en: So sometimes associated as well with fertility, again, because of their kind of the way they're bred and also sometimes a sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 所以有时也与生育力联系在一起，这同样是因为它们的繁育方式，有时也被用作祭品。

sentences.en: So substituted for human sacrifice, sometimes they will sacrifice pigeons almost precisely because they're seen as pure.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为人类献祭的替代品，有时人们会献祭鸽子，几乎正是因为它们被视为纯洁的。

sentences.en: And so it's making this great sacrifice to kill a pigeon.
sentences.zh: 所以杀死一只鸽子是一项重大的牺牲。

sentences.en: Could I just mention two of my favourite classical writers?
sentences.zh: 我能提一下我最喜欢的两位古典作家吗？

sentences.en: Here we go.
sentences.zh: 来了。

sentences.en: We only knew this was coming.
sentences.zh: 我们就知道这要来了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So first, Herodotus, first great historian, Greek historian.
sentences.zh: 首先是希罗多德，第一位伟大的历史学家，希腊历史学家。

sentences.en: I don't know if you've come across this, Gordon.

sentences.en: And Herodotus has a theory that these were not actually doves, but they were priestesses who'd been kidnapped as slaves and taken away.

sentences.en: And he says, the reason for this is to people in Libya and in Greece, the barbarous language of these Egyptian priestesses must have sounded like doves.

sentences.en: And he says, how else to explain the obvious impossibility of a talking dove, which is, you know, the Sandbrookian tone of scepticism right in the very beginnings of history.
sentences.zh: 他说，除此之外，怎么能解释会说话的鸠这一明显的不可思议之处呢？这（也就是历史最开端处桑布鲁克式的怀疑论调）。

sentences.en: The claim of the Dodonians that the dove was black surely signifies that the woman was an Egyptian.
sentences.zh: 多东那人声称鸠是黑色的，这无疑意味着那个女人是埃及人。

sentences.en: So there's Herodotus getting to work on doves.

sentences.zh: 所以他们会把鸽子带到尼罗河上游，如果尼罗河发洪水，他们就会放飞鸽子，鸽子飞回家并向人们发出警告。

sentences.en: But then the first time we start to see the kind of use of it militarily does seem to be, that we know of at least, is around the Roman period.

sentences.zh: 因此，他们迫切想要了解被占领的法国和低地国家内部正在发生的事情，并摸清形势。

sentences.en: And so this intelligence operation is proposed.
sentences.zh: 于是便提出了这个情报行动。

sentences.en: And it comes out, or through a very obscure branch of British intelligence.
sentences.zh: 它来自英国情报部门的一个极其冷门的部门。

sentences.en: You've heard of MI5, you've heard of MI6.
sentences.zh: 你听说过军情五处，你听说过军情六处。

sentences.en: This is MI14 subsection D, which runs the Special Continental Pigeon Service.
sentences.zh: 这是军情十四处D分局，它负责管理特别大陆信鸽服务。

sentences.en: And they decide that what you can do is drop pigeons effectively randomly behind enemy lines
sentences.zh: 他们决定，你可以做的是，通过英国皇家空军飞越敌后并空投特工，

sentences.en: by flying over it through the RAF, who are flying and dropping in special agents.
sentences.zh: 基本上随机地将鸽子空投到敌后。

sentences.en: You drop pigeons in canisters.
sentences.zh: 你把鸽子装在圆筒里空投下来。

sentences.en: And attached to the canisters is a note saying, this is a pigeon from Britain.
sentences.zh: 圆筒上附有一张便条，上面写着：这是一只来自英国的鸽子。

sentences.en: And they often put a copy of a resistance newspaper, or sometimes the Daily Mail with it, to prove it had come from Britain.
sentences.zh: 他们经常随身附上一份抵抗运动报纸的复印件，有时还有《每日邮报》，以证明它是从英国来的。

sentences.en: Oh, Dominant Tom.
sentences.zh: 哦，多米南·汤姆。

sentences.en: What a choice.
sentences.zh: 真是一个不错的选择。

sentences.en: And a questionnaire.
sentences.zh: 还有一份问卷。

sentences.en: And the questionnaire was, what are the Germans doing in your area?
sentences.zh: 问卷的内容是：德国人在你们地区在做什​​么？

sentences.en: What are the German troop deployments?
sentences.zh: 德军的兵力部署情况如何？

sentences.en: Have they been on the move?
sentences.zh: 他们有没有在调动？

sentences.en: What's German morale like?
sentences.zh: 德国人的士气怎么样？

sentences.en: What's the food situation?
sentences.zh: 食物情况如何？

sentences.en: Even what's the reception of the BBC, because they were kind of interested in knowing that.
sentences.zh: 甚至包括BBC的收听情况如何，因为他们对此也挺感兴趣。

sentences.en: A series of kind of questions for people to gather intelligence from ordinary people in occupied Europe.
sentences.zh: 这是一系列问题，旨在从被占领的欧洲的普通人那里收集情报。

sentences.en: And they relied on these pigeons being effectively donated by ordinary pigeon fancies in Britain,
sentences.zh: 他们依靠这些实际上由英国普通养鸽爱好者捐赠的鸽子，

sentences.en: who would give their pigeons to the army and to MI14D, and who would then drop them through the RAF, and then wait and see what they got back on return flights.
sentences.zh: 他们将自己的鸽子交给军队和军情十四处D分局，然后由英国皇家空军空投，接着等待并观察返程航班上能带回什么。

sentences.en: What do they get back?
sentences.zh: 他们带回了什么？

sentences.en: Well, they get back this, you know, and I found this file in the National Archives, which full of these pink slips, and reading them is really powerful, because they're just from
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们带回了这些，你知道的，我在国家档案馆里发现了这个档案，里面装满了粉红色的纸条，阅读它们非常有冲击力，因为它们仅仅来自

sentences.en: ordinary people in rural France, particularly also Belgium, the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 法国农村的普通人，特别是还有比利时和荷兰。

sentences.en: And they range from people going, you know, not much to see here, but please come and liberate
sentences.zh: 他们的内容从人们说，你知道的，这里没什么好看的，但请尽快来解放

sentences.en: us soon to talk about the food supply to rich intelligence about what's going on in their area.
sentences.zh: 我们，到谈论食物供应，再到关于他们地区发生事情的丰富情报。

sentences.en: There's one particular message, which I kind of got obsessed by, which was message 37, which came from Belgium, and had this amazing amount of detail.
sentences.zh: 有一个特别的信息让我有些着迷，那就是第37号信息，它来自比利时，包含了极其惊人的细节。

sentences.en: And if you imagine, it had to be fitted on, you know, on a, on a, you know, a piece of paper about the size of a large postage stamp, which could then go into a tube and fit around
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，它必须被塞进，你知道的，一张大约大邮票大小的纸条上，然后放进一个小管子里，套在

sentences.en: a pigeon's leg.
sentences.zh: 鸽子的腿上。

sentences.en: And yet it produced about a dozen pages of intelligence, because someone had written
sentences.zh: 然而它却产出了大约十几页的情报，因为有人用

sentences.en: in the most tiny way, it was actually a Catholic priest, who'd learned calligraphy while a missionary
sentences.zh: 极其微小的字体书写，实际上那是一个天主教神父，他在中国做传教士时

sentences.en: in China, to write in huge detail, intelligence about German deployments and where German headquarters were.
sentences.zh: 学过书法，他用极大的细节写下了关于德军部署和德国指挥部所在地的情报。

sentences.en: And in the archives, you know, this message gets shown to Churchill, and Churchill is shown that message personally.
sentences.zh: 在档案馆里，你知道的，这条消息被拿给丘吉尔看，丘吉尔亲自看到了那条消息。

sentences.en: And, you know, in a way, I found that fascinating, because Churchill himself wouldn't, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，某种程度上，我发现这很迷人，因为丘吉尔本人不会，你知道的，

sentences.en: he didn't need to know that specific piece of intelligence, you know, that's, that's not his job.
sentences.zh: 他不需要知道那条具体的情报，你知道的，那不是他的工作。

sentences.en: So why was he shown it?
sentences.zh: 那为什么还要给他看呢？

sentences.en: Well, the answer was, it embodied that spirit of resistance, which Churchill so believed in and so wanted to foster in Europe.
sentences.zh: 答案是，它体现了丘吉尔深信不疑并极力想在欧洲培养的那种抵抗精神。

sentences.en: And this was a sign that there were people there in occupied Europe who were willing to risk their lives by sending messages back to Britain through a pigeon with intelligence,
sentences.zh: 这表明被占领的欧洲有人愿意冒着生命危险，通过带着情报的鸽子把消息送回英国，

sentences.en: because they wanted to resiSt.
sentences.zh: 因为他们想要抵抗。

sentences.en: So it was this powerful bond was created through the pigeon between Britain and people in occupied
sentences.zh: 因此，通过鸽子，在英国与被占领的欧洲人民之间建立了一种强大的纽带，

sentences.en: Europe, particularly in that early stage of the war.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在战争的那个早期阶段。

sentences.en: But also, Gordon, presumably, because it kind of shows the can-do spirit, the innovative qualities that Churchill was really into, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 而且戈登，据推测，这也是因为这有点展示了丘吉尔非常热衷的那种敢做精神和创新特质，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, he was kind of obsessed with coming up with weird wheezes schemes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他有点痴迷于想出各种古怪的绝妙主意。

sentences.en: He likes a wheeze, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他喜欢出点子，不是吗？

sentences.en: He likes a wheeze and a clever intelligence operation.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢出点子和聪明的谍报行动。

sentences.en: And what's interesting is even the kind of scientific bonds in British intelligence.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，甚至还包括英国情报部门里的那种科学纽带。

sentences.en: So R.V.
sentences.zh: 所以拉尔夫·维克托·琼斯

sentences.en: Jones, who's the famous figure involved in MI6 and the air ministry, realises he can use these pigeons.
sentences.zh: ——这位参与军情六处和空军部的著名人物——意识到他可以利用这些鸽子。

sentences.en: So he asked for a question on this questionnaire about, have you seen any kind of strange structures
sentences.zh: 因此他在问卷中加入了一个问题：你有没有见过任何奇怪的结构，

sentences.en: with rotating features?
sentences.zh: 带有旋转特征的？

sentences.en: And what he's looking for are German radar stations.
sentences.zh: 他要找的是德国雷达站。

sentences.en: And he realises that people will spot something strange.
sentences.zh: 他意识到人们会发现一些奇怪的东西。

sentences.en: They won't know what it is, but they're so unusual that they will be able to identify these radar stations, which are often hidden in rural locations, which is the kind of places
sentences.zh: 他们可能不知道那是什么，但它们太不寻常了，以至于能够识别出这些通常隐藏在乡村地点的雷达站，而这些地方

sentences.en: these pigeons normally get dropped.
sentences.zh: 正是这些鸽子通常被空投的地方。

sentences.en: And a number of German radar stations are spotted purely thanks to Operation Columba and then destroyed, which protects RAF planes.
sentences.zh: 纯粹由于“哥伦比亚行动”，许多德国雷达站被发现并随后被摧毁，这保护了英国皇家空军的飞机。

sentences.en: It's the same, actually, with V1 and V2 launch sites.
sentences.zh: 事实上，V1和V2发射基地也是如此。

sentences.en: Again, you know, these very modern weapons of war are spotted thanks to intelligence, which is brought back through the pigeons.
sentences.zh: 同样，你知道，这些非常现代的战争武器是通过情报被发现的，而这些情报是由鸽子带回来的。

sentences.en: And Gordon, are the Germans doing the same?
sentences.zh: 戈登，那德国人也在这么做吗？

sentences.en: Are they using pigeons?
sentences.zh: 他们也在用鸽子吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So they actually, in true German style, are far more organised about their pigeon use than the kind of a slightly haphazard British volunteer operation.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，本着真正的德国风格，他们在鸽子的使用上比英国那种略显杂乱的志愿者行动要有组织得多。

sentences.en: But one of the fun stories of the war is, so early on, there's this war.
sentences.zh: 但战争中有趣的轶事之一是，在战争初期。

sentences.en: There's a worry that British Columba pigeons and other pigeons being used in the war are going to be killed by peregrine falcons on the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 人们担心英国“哥伦比亚”鸽以及战争中使用的其他鸽子会被海岸上的游隼捕杀。

sentences.en: And so they decide that to protect the intelligence coming in from the birds, they're going to have to kill the peregrine falcons.
sentences.zh: 因此他们决定，为了保护这些鸟类带回的情报，他们不得不杀死游隼。

sentences.en: And so MI5 sets up one of the few units I've ever discovered, which does have a licence to kill, which is the Falcon Destruction Unit.
sentences.zh: 于是军情五处成立了我发现的极少数拥有杀戮执照的部门之一，即游隼消灭部队。

sentences.en: And its job, which is the Falcon Destruction Unit, is five guys who go round in a big American
sentences.zh: 它的任务——也就是游隼消灭部队——是由五个人组成，他们开着一辆美国大卡车

sentences.en: Packard car with a caravan on the back and go round the cliffs of Britain killing falcons, basically.
sentences.zh: 后面挂着一辆大篷车，基本上就是绕着英国的悬崖去杀隼。

sentences.en: And their job is to protect the pigeons.
sentences.zh: 他们的任务是保护鸽子。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, one falls off a cliff to his death.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，其中一人从悬崖上掉下去摔死了。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of tragicomic story.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个有点悲喜剧的故事。

sentences.en: But then in that piece of kind of absurdity, which could only be kind of the British wartime
sentences.zh: 但随后，在这种只有英国战时

sentences.en: intelligence service, they then suddenly get worried at MI5 that actually the Germans might
sentences.zh: 情报部门才有的荒诞情节中，军情五处突然开始担心，德国人实际上可能

sentences.en: be sending pigeons out of Britain and that they might be using pigeons for undercover agents in Britain to send back intelligence to Germany.
sentences.zh: 会把鸽子从英国放飞出去，并且他们可能会利用鸽子让潜伏在英国的特工向德国发回情报。

sentences.en: So they suddenly realise, particularly, they spot some pigeons flying fast over the Silly
sentences.zh: 所以他们突然意识到，特别是他们发现一些鸽子正快速飞越锡利

sentences.en: Isles towards Europe.
sentences.zh: 群岛朝欧洲飞去。

sentences.en: And they're like, Nazi pigeons, we've got to stop them.
sentences.zh: 他们当时想：“纳粹鸽子，我们必须阻止它们。”

sentences.en: So in a way of fact...
sentences.zh: 所以事实上……

sentences.en: How do you identify a Nazi pigeon?
sentences.zh: 你怎么辨别一只纳粹鸽子？

sentences.en: I've got the swastikas.
sentences.zh: 我有纳粹万字旗。

sentences.en: Just to be clear, they're doing salutes while they're flying.
sentences.zh: 澄清一下，它们在飞行时还在行纳粹礼。

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: So in one of those fantastic wartime reversals from having a Falcon Destruction Unit, they then
sentences.zh: 因此，在经历了一次精彩的战时反转——从拥有一个游隼消灭部队开始，他们随后

sentences.en: decide they need a Falcon Unit to hunt Nazi pigeons and set one up and get someone who has got a peregrine falcon trained to hunt Nazi pigeons.
sentences.zh: 决定需要一个游隼部队来猎杀纳粹鸽子，于是成立了一个，并找了一个训练有素、会用游隼猎杀纳粹鸽子的人。

sentences.en: And this team from MI5 goes onto the Silly Isles in the summer and they sit on the golf course
sentences.zh: 这个来自军情五处的团队在夏天前往锡利群岛，他们坐在锡利群岛的高尔夫球场上

sentences.en: of the Silly Isles with a Falcon on their wrist, as you might have seen, ready to hunt pigeons.
sentences.zh: 手腕上戴着一只猎鹰，正如你可能见过的那样，准备猎杀鸽子。

sentences.en: And they kill pigeons, but the only pigeons they kill are plucky British pigeons.
sentences.zh: 他们确实杀鸽子，但他们杀的唯一的鸽子是勇敢的英国鸽子。

sentences.en: So they never find a Nazi pigeon?
sentences.zh: 所以他们从来没有找到过纳粹鸽子？

sentences.en: Not a single Nazi pigeon.
sentences.zh: 连一只纳粹鸽子都没有。

sentences.en: There must be some way they could have done a coup or test to see if their coup had got a German accent, a German-accented pigeon.
sentences.zh: 总有一种方法可以让他们进行一次政变或测试，看看他们的政变对象是不是一只带着德国口音的鸽子。

sentences.en: No swastikas on the pigeon, no friend or foe identifier on the pigeon.
sentences.zh: 鸽子上没有万字旗，鸽子上也没有敌我识别标志。

sentences.en: So it's not the most successful wartime operation, it's fair to say, but, you know, emblematic of the realities of war.
sentences.zh: 所以可以说这不是最成功的战时行动，但你知道，它是战争现实的象征。

sentences.en: And does, Gordon, does this division of MI5 still exist?
sentences.zh: 戈登，军情五处的这个部门现在还存在吗？

sentences.en: We wouldn't know, wouldn't we, Tom?
sentences.zh: 我们不会知道的，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: If it was, Tom.
sentences.zh: 如果它还在的话，汤姆。

sentences.en: I think it was B-1-3-C of MI5.
sentences.zh: 我想它是军情五处的B-1-3-C。

sentences.en: It might secretly still be going on.
sentences.zh: 它可能还在秘密运行。

sentences.en: It might still, yeah.
sentences.zh: 可能还在，对。

sentences.en: But there are other heroic pigeons, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 但还有其他英雄鸽子，对吧？

sentences.en: So there's a pigeon, I believe, called Winky.
sentences.zh: 所以我相信有一只名叫温基的鸽子。

sentences.en: Winky's a great hero of the Second World War?
sentences.zh: 温基是二战的伟大英雄？

sentences.en: Yeah, because they also use them on, the RAF gives pigeons to planes, particularly going over the sea, in case they crash, in case they ditch.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为他们也在飞机上使用鸽子，英国皇家空军会把鸽子交给飞机，特别是飞越大海的飞机，以防它们坠毁，以防它们迫降。

sentences.en: And the radios don't work or there's a problem.
sentences.zh: 如果电台坏了或者出了问题。

sentences.en: Then you release a pigeon with your coordinates.
sentences.zh: 然后你就可以放飞一只带着你坐标的鸽子。

sentences.en: And Winky is a very famous case because the plane tries to radio where it is, it ditches.
sentences.zh: 温基是一个非常著名的例子，因为飞机试图用无线电报告它在哪里，然后它迫降了。

sentences.en: Winky actually gets free without a message, flies home, but covered in oil from the ditching.
sentences.zh: 温基实际上在没有携带纸条的情况下脱身了，飞回家了，但身上沾满了迫降时的油污。

sentences.en: And so the loft owner and the RAF work out that this is a pigeon from the plane that ditched.
sentences.zh: 于是鸽舍主人和英国皇家空军弄清了这是一只来自迫降飞机的鸽子。

sentences.en: And they work out, based on the speed with which it flew, roughly where that plane might be, and then locate the plane and save the crew in their dinghy.
sentences.zh: 根据它的飞行速度，他们推算出那架飞机大致可能在哪里，然后定位了飞机并救出了救生艇上的机组人员。

sentences.en: That's a good story.
sentences.zh: 这是个好故事。

sentences.en: Does Winky get a medal?
sentences.zh: 温基获得勋章了吗？

sentences.en: Winky is one of those who is heavily decorated.
sentences.zh: 温基是那些获得大量勋章的人之一。

sentences.en: And I think he's giving a big dinner at the RAF.
sentences.zh: 我想空军为它举办了一场盛大的晚宴。

sentences.en: He's winking, he's winking.
sentences.zh: 它在眨眼，它在眨眼。

sentences.en: And that's why he's called Winky.
sentences.zh: 这就是它为什么叫温基。

sentences.en: But the thought is he's actually so exhausted still.
sentences.zh: 但大家认为它其实还是太累了。

sentences.en: He's never recovered from his flight.
sentences.zh: 它从未从飞行中恢复过来。

sentences.en: That's why he's winking.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它在眨眼。

sentences.en: But he's known as Winky.
sentences.zh: 但它被称为温基。

sentences.en: If I was a pigeon, I'd be very suspicious of being invited to a dinner at an RAF.
sentences.zh: 如果我是一只鸽子，对于被邀请去参加空军晚宴这件事，我会非常怀疑。

sentences.en: Wouldn't you?
sentences.zh: 难道你不会吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I'd be very angry.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我会非常生气。

sentences.en: I'd want to see the menu before Speckled Jim.
sentences.zh: 在看到斑点吉姆的菜单之前，我会想先看看菜单。

sentences.en: I'm afraid that's what happens to lots of the Columba pigeons.
sentences.zh: 恐怕这就是许多哥伦比亚鸽子的下场。

sentences.en: You know, they're dropped in the French countryside and hungry French farmers roast them with peas.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它们被空投到法国乡村，然后饥饿的法国农民把它们和豌豆一起烤着吃了。

sentences.en: Oh, that's braw.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太棒了。

sentences.en: A pigeon pitches up with a copy of the Daily Mail.
sentences.zh: 一只鸽子带着一份《每日邮报》飞来。

sentences.en: And the first few French crews eat it.
sentences.zh: 前几个法国机组人员把它吃掉了。

sentences.en: Confirming all your darker suspicions of France.
sentences.zh: 这证实了你对法国最阴暗的猜测。

sentences.en: So, Gordon, after the Second World War, do pigeons continue to have any role in intelligence or not?
sentences.zh: 所以，戈登，二战后，鸽子在情报工作中是否继续发挥任何作用？

sentences.en: Well, so after the war, there is this, again, when I went through the National Archives,
sentences.zh: 嗯，战后确实有这样一件事，当我翻阅国家档案馆时，

sentences.en: the things you find at Kew, but was a file about the Joint Intelligence Committee subcommittee on pigeons, whose minutes I read studiously.

sentences.en: In which there is quite a serious debate about, you know, whether pigeons, whether a pigeon research capability should be kept.

sentences.en: And I was fascinated to see one of the artefacts they have is a stuffed pigeon with a tiny camera on its cheSt.

sentences.zh: 所以我想提出一个问题，在我们进入现代之际，你知道，

sentences.en: And the reason was that they were concerned that in the event of some kind of cyber attack, which took out their communications, they could then rely on pigeons.

sentences.en: And it got me, you know, worried and wondering, you know, whether we are pigeon prepared as a nation or is there?

sentences.en: Yeah, because it goes back to my point, you know, pigeons, you know, superheroes of history, you know, saved us from the kind of flood through the Second World War.

sentences.en: But yeah, I mean, you know, the breeding of those pigeons to kind of, a bit like racehorses, to kind of breed the best pigeons.

sentences.en: And he kind of draws this analogy between artificial selection and natural selection.

sentences.en: And so still the kind of breeding the fastest pigeon or the best pigeon or breeding the most beautiful pigeon.
sentences.zh: 所以依然是繁育最快的鸽子、最好的鸽子，或者繁育最漂亮的鸽子。

sentences.en: You know, so there's always been this thing about pigeon fancying where you breed these kind of beautiful looking birds.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，所以一直以来都有这种养鸽爱好，你繁育出这些外表美丽的鸟类。

sentences.en: So, Gordon, we've looked at the kind of the cultural uses of the pigeon, the way that it's kind of in form mythology and so on.

sentences.zh: 我们回顾了人类在历史长河中对鸽子的种种利用。

sentences.zh: 最后一个主题传达了人类与动物界关系的更深层次真相，

sentences.en: In the billions.
sentences.zh: 成百上千亿。

sentences.en: And people would say it would sound like Niagara Falls, you know, when they moved, you know, and you'd almost feel the earth shake because they were so enormous.

sentences.en: Could I just read from John James Audubon, you know, the great ornithologist, American ornithologist, writing in 1813.
sentences.zh: 我能读一下约翰·詹姆斯·奥杜 Audubon 的文字吗，就是那位伟大的鸟类学家，美国鸟类学家，写于1813年。

sentences.en: And he describes standing underneath the passenger pigeons going paSt.

sentences.en: And the continued buzz of wings had a tendency to lull my senses to repose.
sentences.zh: 翅膀持续的嗡嗡声有一种让我昏昏欲睡的魔力。

sentences.en: And he talks about the pigeons were still passing in undiminished numbers and continue to do so for three days in succession.
sentences.zh: 他提到，鸽子仍然以不减的规模飞过，并且连续三天都是如此。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of absolutely stunning spectacle.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对是一种令人震撼的壮观景象。

sentences.en: The sun blocked out for three days at a time by these passing flocks of pigeons.
sentences.zh: 这些飞过的鸽群连续三天遮天蔽日。

sentences.en: Yeah.
